episode_summary: Barely Informed News opened its Monday broadcast with Pepito's producer cam intro and a chaotic pre-show featuring a phantom 'hype crane' and a brief AI Rooney segment that devolved into sexual and racial commentary before being muted. The core News desk covered Keir Starmer's resignation, escalating Iran-Israel ceasefire tensions, Trump's reflecting pool controversy, and a viral beaver flood-control story, before transitioning into a therapy segment with Dr. Chath and concluding with a CryptoZeu$ gaming dispatch featuring Operation Epic Furious Straight and a Gooters chicken sponsorship.

segments.title: Pepito Intro & Phantom Hype Crane
segments.notes: Pepito opens the show from the producer cam, rambles about subs, time travel, and a phantom 'hype crane' that may or may not exist. Features cat projections, merch discussion, and a brief mention of Operation Epic Furious Straight.

segments.title: Starmer Resigns, Iran Ceasefire Chaos & Beaver Flood Heroes
segments.notes: Case covers Keir Starmer's resignation as Labour leader, ongoing Iran-Israel ceasefire negotiations with JD Vance involved, Trump's reflecting pool Truth Social posts, and a heartwarming story about beavers controlling urban flooding in London. Also touches on Steam Deck pricing and vaccine coverage.

segments.title: AI Rooney's Unhinged Grievance Spew
segments.notes: Case attempts to activate AI Rooney for a grievance segment, but Rooney produces increasingly offensive content involving sexual references, racial commentary, and bizarre tangents about soup, beards, and cavemen. Case repeatedly mutes Rooney and tries to reprompt him, ultimately concluding the segment was mostly unscathed.

segments.title: Therapy Session with Dr. Chath
segments.notes: Case announces a therapy segment instead of Trip on the Street, sitting with Dr. Chath who provides confusing advice involving wrestling references, dance moves, and bizarre tangents. Features Kendall's ghostly appearance and discussions about banning/raiding viewers.

segments.title: Operation Epic Furious Straight Gaming Dispatch
segments.notes: Brandon (CryptoZeu$) takes over for a gaming segment playing Operation Epic Furious Straight, a browser-based game featuring Trump, Iran, and various political figures. Features heavy mother interruptions, Gooters chicken sponsorship, and absurd gameplay involving Truth Social posts and drone strikes.

storylines.beat: Case attempts to activate AI Rooney for a grievance segment, but Rooney produces increasingly offensive content involving sexual references, racial commentary, and bizarre tangents. Case repeatedly mutes Rooney and tries to reprompt him, ultimately concluding the segment was mostly unscathed but noting Rooney's continued misbehavior.
During the therapy segment, Case accidentally raids someone he was trying to ban, leading to a discussion about his typing difficulties and the mods having to handle the situation.
Case discusses various merch submissions including separate Munch & Crum shirts, bin hoodies, and a potential tux shirt design, noting they are 115 subs away from any t-shirt drops.

storylines.storyline: Operation Epic Furious Straight gaming segment
storylines.beat: Case announces a gaming segment featuring Operation Epic Furious Straight, which Brandon plays from his bedroom while his mother interrupts with various demands and commentary.

lore_notes.fact: AI Rooney has been retired due to offensive outputs but Case still attempts to activate it, noting it has been 'misbehaving' and producing racist and sexual content. Case mentions Rooney has 'over a hundred training parameters' and tries to use a 'Grok' model as an alternative.

Dr. Chath is a therapist who appears during Case's therapy segment, providing confusing advice involving wrestling references, dance moves, and bizarre tangents. He wears a hat that is 'way too big for his head' and occasionally disappears or becomes unresponsive.

Kendelle is Case's girlfriend and on-air contributor who appears as a ghost during the therapy segment, walking through the studio to her own signature theme music. She lives in the therapist's office sometimes and follows 'Harry Potter rules' for apparition.

Brandon's Mother makes her presence known entirely via muffled screaming through the drywall during his gaming segments, frequently interrupting with demands for food, commentary on his gameplay, and references to Gooters chicken.

Gooters is a chicken wing sponsor that provides wet chicken products, including a 30-person party plan subscription. Brandon's mother frequently references Gooters during his gaming segments, and the network has an official sponsorship relationship with them.

Hype Train is a high-velocity musical correspondent who travels with his Panther companion. During this broadcast, he confesses to cheating on his Panther girlfriend for seven years and discusses his emotional state regarding the relationship.

Pepito is the canine executive producer who opens the broadcast from the producer cam, thanking subscribers and providing station announcements. He mentions having 'light time travel' over the weekend that is 'kind of unresolved.'

Case Blackwell is the lead anchor and managing editor who presides over the entire broadcast. He discusses his VPN causing access restrictions to news sites, his 4K film collection habits, and his difficulty with Twitch raid/ban functions.
Munch and Crum are senior debate analysts who are mentioned in the context of potential separate merchandise shirts, with Case noting they are 'the longest standing thing other than chat.'
Peter Gibbon is a disgraced former producer who now inhabits the studio wall crawlspaces as a news stowaway. He is referenced in a merch submission titled 'Leave it to Peter, starring Peter Gibbon.'
Jeb Nogget is the host of 'How To with Jeb' who is joined by his deceased father trapped inside a wooden board. He is referenced in merch brainstorming as 'the two Jebs' inside all of us.
